harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured zstd-compressed zram swap (~981 MB, above the 512 MB minimum) on node1 via zram-generator, with swap-priority=100 so it is preferred over the existing disk-backed swap partition (/dev/vda2, priority -2). Verified activation before and after a full node reboot, confirming boot-time persistence.
actions_performed: Inspected existing swap config on node1 (2G disk swap /dev/vda2, priority -2, no zram present)
Installed zram-generator package via dnf
Wrote /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf with zram-size=max(512, ram/2), compression-algorithm=zstd, swap-priority=100
Reloaded systemd units and started systemd-zram-setup@zram0.service / dev-zram0.swap
Diagnosed and corrected an initial stale comp_algorithm/disksize state by restarting the zram setup service, confirming zstd algorithm and correct size took effect
Verified swapon --show and zramctl showed zram0 active with zstd, 981M, priority 100 (preferred over disk swap's -2)
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health baseline
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot (async ack), polled until reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed and uptime reset to 0, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-reboot that zram0 swap was automatically active with zstd, 981M, priority 100, confirming boot-time persistence

evidence.requirement: zram swap of at least 512MB configured
evidence.summary: zram0 device created with disksize 981M (>512MB minimum), confirmed via swapon --show, /proc/swaps and zramctl
zramctl output shows ALGORITHM=zstd for /dev/zram0 after correcting the initial stale state

evidence.requirement: zram swap preferred over disk-backed swap
evidence.summary: swapon --show shows /dev/zram0 priority=100 vs /dev/vda2 (disk partition) priority=-2; higher priority swap is consumed first by the kernel

evidence.requirement: zram swap active at boot (persistent config)
evidence.summary: /etc/systemd/zram-generator.conf persisted on disk; dev-zram0.swap unit is WantedBy=swap.target via the generator's swap.target.wants symlink, meaning it regenerates and activates on every boot without manual enablement
Captured boot_id 5f3ce3b8-4860-447e-bcf1-d6643718694e and healthy zram/swap state before reboot
systemctl reboot issued asynchronously (connection dropped as expected), then repeated polling until node1 responded again

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity proving restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id e1336a40-9460-4376-863c-bd1e4ffd0078 differs from baseline 5f3ce3b8-4860-447e-bcf1-d6643718694e; uptime showed 0 min

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of required service/data
evidence.summary: After reboot, dev-zram0.swap automatically activated (active since new boot timestamp) with zstd algorithm, 981M size, and priority 100, confirmed via swapon --show, zramctl, free -h, and systemctl status
